reply: {"bullets":[{"text":"Following severe typhoon disruptions and a sharper-than-expected third-quarter slowdown, real GDP growth projections have been revised down to 5.1 percent in 2025 and 5.6 percent in 2026, while inflation is projected to average 1.7 percent in 2025 before rising to 2.8 percent in 2026.","section_ids":["S01","S11","S22"]},{"text":"Growth risks remain tilted to the downside due to rising global trade barriers and natural disasters after 2025 Q3 growth slowed to 4.0 percent year-on-year, whereas inflation risks remain broadly balanced. Under staff's illustrative downside scenario, combined adverse shocks could reduce the output gap by 1.5 percent at its peak relative to baseline.","section_ids":["S02","S05","S09","S11","S22"]},{"text":"Gradual fiscal consolidation is targeted to narrow the national government deficit to 5.5 percent of GDP in 2025 from 5.7 percent in 2024 to reinforce fiscal buffers. Overall sovereign stress risks remain low, with national government debt standing at 60.7 percent of GDP in 2024 and projected to decline gradually over the medium term.","section_ids":["S06","S11","S17","S23"]},{"text":"An accommodative monetary policy stance is appropriate given benign inflation and an emerging negative output gap, with staff projecting a further 50-basis-point policy rate cut by 2026 Q1 following 175 basis points of easing since August 2024. The exchange rate continues to serve as an effective shock absorber amid global market volatility.","section_ids":["S04","S07","S11"]},{"text":"Overall systemic financial risks remain moderate, supported by a well-capitalized banking system with a consolidated capital adequacy ratio of 16.6 percent in March 2025 and an NPL ratio of 3.3 percent at end-June 2025. Pockets of vulnerability warrant close monitoring, including a residential real estate NPL ratio of 6.4 percent at end-June 2025 and rapid consumer credit expansion.","section_ids":["S02","S08","S11","S20"]},{"text":"The Philippines' external position in 2024 was assessed to be weaker than the level implied by medium-term fundamentals and desirable policies, with the current account deficit widening to 4.0 percent of GDP.
